sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the rescue] The UAE National Guard's Coast Guard rescued 22 people of Arab nationality after a fire broke out aboard a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman; all 22 received first aid and are in stable condition. The National Guard statement (on X) says specialised teams located the vessel and evacuated everyone aboard; it names neither the vessel nor the cause of the fire. [UNVERIFIED -- the link to the mine claim] No official statement links this burning ship to the two tankers the IRGC Navy says hit mines in/near the Strait of Hormuz (recorded 0700-02). Al Jazeera's liveblog notes only that the rescue 'came after' the IRGC claim; the National Guard statement calls the vessel both a 'cargo ship' and 'the tanker'. The ship could be one of the two IRGC-claimed tankers, a third vessel, or unrelated -- identity is unresolved. [ATTRIBUTION ONLY -- tugboat] Times Now's liveblog (07:28 IST = 05:58 ) says 'two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire'; Times Now has NO declared tier in the registry, so the tugboat detail counts for nothing toward corroboration and is not recorded as fact. [COUNTEREVIDENCE / DO-NOT-CONFLATE] Khaleej Times notes the Coast Guard saved a different crew of 22 last month (MT GEM No. 2, Arabian Gulf) -- a separate incident. The Oct 31 Oman rescue of 25 sailors from the Panamanian-flagged RITI is also a different incident (different country, count and date); a blogspot recirculation this hour presents it as current -- re-date trap, see triage 0800-03(g). [PORTWATCH BACKBONE -- STALE] IMF PortWatch snapshot portwatch-2026-11-08.json (fetched 03:06 ) is STALE: latest observation 2026-11-01 (7-day lag). Counted Hormuz transits on 2026-11-01: 1 transit; 7-day average 4.43/day vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day (5.2% of baseline). Cite only with the observation date and the stale flag; never as a live figure.
sections.what_verified: Rescue confirmed by the primary source (UAE National Guard, T1 STATE) and carried by 3 additional tiered families (Al Jazeera T2, Gulf News T3, Times of Israel T3). The link between the rescued ship and the IRGC mine claim is UNVERIFIED -- no official statement makes it.
sections.what_disputed: No official statement links the rescued ship to the IRGC's two tankers; vessel unnamed; fire cause unspecified. Khaleej Times' separate 22-person rescue last month (MT GEM No. 2) and Oman's Oct 31 RITI rescue (25) are different incidents -- do not merge counts.
sections.why_matters: 22 saved -- but nobody will name the ship. The rescue proves a fire happened in the Gulf of Oman; the identity gap is the story: the vessel at the centre of the mine claim still has no name, no flag, no confirmed link.

totw_analysis: Our read: 22 saved -- but nobody will name the ship. The rescue proves a fire happened in the Gulf of Oman; the identity gap is the story: the vessel at the centre of the mine claim still has no name, no flag, no confirmed link. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Was the burning ship one of the IRGC's 'violating' tankers -- or a third vessel nobody has named? Rescue vs blockade: who protects crews when both sides are shooting at shipping?
